topics.title: The Constitution
topics.summary: The U.S. Constitution was written in 1787 at the Constitutional Convention in Philadelphia and signed on September 17 of that year. It opens with the words "We the People" and sets up the federal government in three branches. It is the supreme law of the land, and it has been changed 27 times through amendments.
topics.simpleEnglish: The Constitution is the most important law in the United States. It was written in 1787 in Philadelphia. It starts with the words "We the People." It creates the government. It has 27 amendments, which are changes.

topics.title: The Declaration of Independence
topics.summary: The Continental Congress adopted the Declaration of Independence on July 4, 1776. Thomas Jefferson wrote most of the text. The document announced that the thirteen American colonies were free from Great Britain and stated that all people have rights to "Life, Liberty and the pursuit of Happiness."
topics.simpleEnglish: The Declaration of Independence was adopted on July 4, 1776. Thomas Jefferson wrote it. It said the colonies were free from Britain. It says people have the right to life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness.

sources.title: The Declaration of Independence: A History

topics.title: The Bill of Rights
topics.summary: The Bill of Rights is the name for the first ten amendments to the Constitution. They were ratified on December 15, 1791. The First Amendment protects freedom of religion, speech, the press, assembly, and the right to petition the government. The other amendments protect rights such as trial by jury.
topics.simpleEnglish: The Bill of Rights is the first ten amendments to the Constitution. It became law in 1791. The First Amendment protects freedom of speech and freedom of religion. The Bill of Rights protects the rights of people in the United States.

sources.title: The Bill of Rights: How Did it Happen?

topics.title: The Three Branches of Government
topics.summary: The Constitution divides the federal government into three branches. The legislative branch, Congress, writes the laws and has two parts: the Senate and the House of Representatives. The executive branch, led by the President, carries out the laws. The judicial branch, the Supreme Court and other federal courts, interprets the laws. Each branch can check the others so that no branch becomes too powerful.
topics.simpleEnglish: The government has three parts, called branches. Congress makes the laws. The President carries out the laws. The courts explain the laws. This system is called checks and balances. It stops one branch from having too much power.

topics.title: The Mississippi River
topics.summary: The Mississippi River begins at Lake Itasca in Minnesota and flows about 2,350 miles south to the Gulf of America (also known as the Gulf of Mexico) in Louisiana. Along the way it forms borders in parts of ten states. Together with the Missouri River, which is about 100 miles longer, it is one of the two longest rivers in the United States, and it has long been a route for boats, farm goods, and trade.
topics.simpleEnglish: The Mississippi River is one of the two longest rivers in the United States. It starts in Minnesota. It ends in Louisiana at the Gulf of America, also called the Gulf of Mexico. It touches ten states. Boats carry goods on the river.

topics.title: The Grand Canyon
topics.summary: The Grand Canyon is in northern Arizona, a state on the border with Mexico. The Colorado River has been carving it for five to six million years. The canyon is 277 river miles long, up to 18 miles wide, and about a mile deep. Grand Canyon National Park was established in 1919, and the rocks at the bottom of the canyon are almost two billion years old.
topics.simpleEnglish: The Grand Canyon is in Arizona. The Colorado River made it over millions of years. It is very long, very wide, and about one mile deep. It became a national park in 1919. The rocks at the bottom are almost two billion years old.

sources.title: Grand Canyon National Park: Frequently Asked Questions

topics.title: The Statue of Liberty
topics.summary: The Statue of Liberty stands on Liberty Island in New York Harbor. It was a gift of friendship from the people of France and was dedicated on October 28, 1886. The French sculptor Frédéric Auguste Bartholdi designed the copper statue, which holds a torch and a tablet. Nearby Ellis Island received more than 12 million immigrants between 1892 and 1924, and the statue was among the first things they saw from their ships.
topics.simpleEnglish: The Statue of Liberty is in New York Harbor, on Liberty Island. France gave it to the United States in 1886. The statue holds a torch. Many immigrants saw the statue when they arrived by ship.

topics.title: Washington, D.C.
topics.summary: Washington, D.C. is the capital of the United States. It is not part of any state: D.C. stands for District of Columbia, a federal district. Congress passed the Residence Act in 1790, and President George Washington chose the site the next year, on land ceded by Maryland; the city plan was drawn by Pierre L'Enfant. The White House, the U.S. Capitol, and the Supreme Court are all in the city, along with the memorials of the National Mall.
topics.simpleEnglish: Washington, D.C. is the capital of the United States. It is not in any state. George Washington chose the place for the city. The President lives in the White House there. Congress meets in the Capitol building there.

topics.title: Katherine Johnson
topics.summary: Katherine Johnson (1918–2020) was a mathematician at NASA's Langley Research Center in Hampton, Virginia. She calculated the trajectory for Alan Shepard's 1961 flight, the first American human spaceflight, and in 1962 John Glenn asked that she check the computer's numbers by hand before his orbit of Earth. Her calculations also helped the Apollo program's lunar module link up with the command module orbiting the Moon. In 2015 President Barack Obama awarded her the Presidential Medal of Freedom.
topics.simpleEnglish: Katherine Johnson was a mathematician. She worked for NASA in Virginia. She did the math for the first American space flights. She helped the Apollo missions go to the Moon. In 2015 the President gave her a medal.

topics.title: Apollo 11 and the Moon Landing
topics.summary: Apollo 11 launched from Kennedy Space Center in Florida on July 16, 1969. On July 20, Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin landed the lunar module Eagle on the Moon while Michael Collins, the command module pilot, orbited above them. Armstrong became the first person to walk on the Moon. The crew returned to Earth on July 24, 1969. USCIS lists landing on the Moon as an example of an American innovation.
topics.simpleEnglish: In July 1969, three astronauts flew to the Moon on Apollo 11. Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin walked on the Moon. Michael Collins stayed in the spacecraft. They came back to Earth safely. It was the first time people walked on the Moon.

topics.title: Juneteenth
topics.summary: On June 19, 1865, U.S. Major General Gordon Granger issued General Order No. 3 in Galveston, Texas, announcing that all enslaved people in Texas were free. This came more than two years after the Emancipation Proclamation of January 1, 1863. The day became known as Juneteenth. Texas made it a legal state holiday starting in 1980, and on June 17, 2021, it became a federal holiday, Juneteenth National Independence Day.
topics.simpleEnglish: Juneteenth is June 19. On that day in 1865, soldiers came to Galveston, Texas. They said that enslaved people in Texas were free. Today Juneteenth is a national holiday. It celebrates freedom.

topics.title: Yellowstone National Park
topics.summary: Yellowstone became the first national park in the world when Congress established it on March 1, 1872. Most of the park is in Wyoming, and it reaches into Montana and Idaho, two states that border Canada. It has more than 10,000 hydrothermal features, such as hot springs, mud pots, and geysers, including Old Faithful, and it is home to bison, elk, grizzly bears, and wolves.
topics.simpleEnglish: Yellowstone was the first national park. It opened in 1872. It is mostly in Wyoming. It has hot springs and geysers. Old Faithful is a famous geyser. Bison and bears live in the park.
